summary: The narrator, distraught over his friends' self-interest and his own sense of being crippled since working with Halliday, drives aimlessly around the city and then breaks into Rita Martinez's condo searching for clues to where she has fled. He notices her shelves have dust-outlined gaps despite her denial that anything is missing. Outside, an elderly neighbor with a cane asks whether he is Rita's friend or daughter, mentions government people who had come asking about her after 'the other lady got snatched,' and claims the government murdered Martinez's family, which the narrator finds unlikely.
one_line: A narrator searches for the missing Rita Martinez at her condo, where a suspicious elderly neighbor hints that government agents have been asking about her.
key_facts: The narrator feels his so-called friends only cared about him as suited their own needs.
The narrator says something in his head prevented him from noticing how crippled he was until the work with Halliday.
The narrator drove around the city with an aimless vengeance, running out of gas, refilling the tank, and continuing.
The narrator says Martinez is the only problem he seems to have any shot at solving right now.
The narrator drove to Martinez's condo and broke in, believing Arthur was more observant and would have found anything relevant.
The narrator ran his hand along the dust in front of the empty spaces on Martinez's living room shelves.
Martinez had denied that anything was missing, but the narrator concludes she had clearly been lying.
The condo building has a small paved area behind it with a high fence, lawn furniture, and a portable fire pit.
A little old man with a cane, scraggly white hair, and half his teeth missing asks whether the narrator is a friend of Rita's.
The old man says government people had been at the building asking about Rita when 'the other lady got snatched.'
The old man says he did not tell the government people anything.
The old man claims Rita never talked about family and that it was painful for her.
The old man says he thinks the government murdered Martinez's family because he does not trust them and they watch people.
The narrator finds it highly unlikely the government randomly murdered Martinez's family.
The narrator tells the old man, 'I'm not her daughter.'
